h1:
Koh Phangan Travel Tips
When to go, how to book, what it costs
intro: Koh Phangan is a fun island, no question — but room prices and the general chaos swing with the season and the full moon far more than most people expect. Show up in the wrong week and you could get rained on for the whole trip, or find rooms going for double. We've pulled together everything worth checking before you set off — timing, booking, safety, and what a day actually costs.
chips: 🌕 Check the full moon date first

blocks.html: Koh Phangan sits in the Gulf of Thailand off Surat Thani, between Samui and Koh Tao. Its charm is having two worlds on one island: the south around Haad Rin is all about the party scene, while the north and east are quiet, laid-back, and good for resting up or doing yoga. Before you book your boat ticket, there are just a few things that — if you know them in advance — make the trip a lot smoother.

blocks.text: When to go and what the weather's like

blocks.html: The best weather runs from December through April — clear skies, little rain, calm seas, temperatures around 28-32°C. Easy diving and easy island-hopping by boat. This is peak season in full swing, so it's also the busiest and most expensive, especially from late December through February.

The stretch to avoid if you don't want to gamble on rain is October through November, which is the Gulf of Thailand's rainy season. Heavy downpours come in waves, the sea gets choppy, and some inter-island boat departures may be cancelled. The tail end of the rains can sometimes drag into early December. If you're on a tight budget and can stomach the rain risk, this is when rooms drop hard because it's low season.

items: Dec-Feb — best weather, pleasantly cool, but packed and rooms at their peak. Booking ahead is a must.
Mar-Apr — still dry and sunny, getting hotter. April brings Songkran and another crowd surge.
May-Sep — sun and rain in turns, prices easing off, the sea still good day to day.
Oct-Nov — heaviest rain, roughest seas, cheapest rooms. For travellers who can handle the rain risk.

blocks.title: A small tip
blocks.html: In the rainy season many hotels drop their rates by 50% or more compared to peak. If you can stay flexible and check the forecast before you head out, you can still have a great trip on a much lighter budget.

blocks.text: Full moon nights 2026 — check the date before you book

blocks.html: The Full Moon Party is held at Haad Rin every month on the night of the full moon, and it's the single biggest thing that swings room prices across the whole island. Around full moon nights, rooms fill up fast and prices climb — especially on the Haad Rin side, where you may be required to book a minimum of several nights. If you want to go to the party, lock in your dates clearly first. And if you want to skip it, you still need to check the date so you can plan around it.
The approximate Full Moon Party dates announced for 2026 are 29 Jun · 31 Jul · 28 Aug · 26 Sep · 27 Oct · 24 Nov · 24 Dec, plus an extra New Year countdown party on the night of 31 Dec.

blocks.title: Check before you trust it
blocks.html: Party dates can get pushed back if they fall on a major Buddhist holiday (such as Asalha Puja / the start of Buddhist Lent, or the end of Lent) — the organisers usually shift it to the following night. Before you book flights or rooms, always confirm the real date on the organiser's page. Don't go by the calendar full-moon date alone.
Almost all boats dock at Thong Sala, the island's main pier. There are two main routes in: from the mainland on the Surat Thani side, or a short hop from Koh Samui.

items: From Surat Thani — speedboats from Tapi or Don Sak piers, around 2.5-3 hours, with several departures a day from multiple companies (Lomprayah, Raja, Seatran).
From Koh Samui — boats from Maenam or Bang Rak pier reach Thong Sala very quickly, around 20-40 minutes. Good if you fly into Samui and connect by boat.
From Koh Tao — speedboats heading south to Thong Sala, around 1-1.5 hours. Good for travellers doing all three islands in one go.

blocks.title: Book your boat ahead
blocks.html: During high season (Dec-Apr), full moon nights, and long Thai holiday weekends, boats fill up fast — book your ticket in advance and leave enough buffer for flight and boat connections. Miss the last departure and you could be stuck on the mainland for a night.

blocks.text: How to book a room without slipping up — especially around party nights

blocks.html: Room prices on Koh Phangan swing on three things: season, full moon nights, and location. To be blunt, the same room can cost nearly double in peak versus low season, and around full moon nights Haad Rin is where prices spike and booking conditions get strictest.

items: For full moon nights, book weeks ahead — the Haad Rin side fills fast and often has minimum-stay requirements of several nights. Check the conditions carefully before you hit book.
Want quiet? Pick the north or east side — Thong Nai Pan, Chaloklum, and Srithanu are quieter, and you can still ride over for the party for one night.
Compare across platforms — the same room can vary by date and channel. Compare before you decide.
Have a rainy-season backup plan — if you're travelling during the rain-risk window, picking a free-cancellation room gives you more peace of mind.

blocks.text: Safety you really need to know

blocks.html: Koh Phangan can be a blast, but there are spots where you genuinely need to be careful — especially around motorbikes and drinking. We'll be straight with you, because this is about your own safety.

items: Riding on steep roads — the routes to Haad Rin and Thong Nai Pan are very steep, and sand and gravel on the bends are one of the top causes of accidents. Beginners should ride slowly, use the brakes a lot, and avoid the steep roads if you're not confident.
Wear a helmet and carry a licence — an international driving permit and insurance help a lot if something goes wrong. Police set up checkpoints from time to time.
Never drink and ride — most accidents happen while drunk, especially on the late-night ride back from the party. If you've been drinking, take a taxi or shuttle back.
Watch out at night — roads are dark, with people and dogs crossing and lots of sharp bends. Ride slowly to be safe.

Drink with your wits about you and mind your valuables — party nights are crowded, so carry only the cash you'll use, keep your passport and valuables in the safe, never leave a drink unattended, and go in a group with friends.
Swim with care — during the monsoon the waves are strong and there are currents. Watch the warning flags and don't get in the water drunk.

blocks.title: Bike rental tip
blocks.html: Most motorbike rental shops ask for a cash deposit of 2,000-5,000 THB plus a copy of your passport. Try to hand over a copy rather than your actual passport, and photograph the scratches all around the bike before you take it, to avoid damage claims when you return it.

A Koh Phangan budget stretches anywhere from backpacker to laid-back-with-comforts, depending mainly on the season and your travel style. The figures below are rough estimates per person per day, not including the boat ticket to the island — and they'll climb during high season and full moon nights.

items.name: Motorbike rental
items.blurb: A 125cc bike rents daily at roughly the same rate island-wide; rent by the month and you can negotiate it down a lot. More powerful models (150-155cc) cost more. Top up a little fuel each day.
items.meta: Main way to get around the island

items.name: Hostel / bungalow stay
items.blurb: A dorm bed or simple bungalow on the quiet side; low-season rates are clearly cheaper than peak. On full moon nights Haad Rin gets pricier and often has multi-night minimum stays.

items.name: Local-restaurant food
items.blurb: Curry-over-rice, pad krapow, noodles from Thong Sala market and roadside shops — you'll eat well on an easy budget. Eat at the foreigner-oriented spots in the tourist areas and it goes up.

items.name: Cafés / tourist restaurants
items.blurb: Coffee cafés, smoothie bowls, and Western restaurants around Srithanu and Thong Sala. Noticeably pricier than local spots, but the atmosphere is nice.

items.name: Snorkelling / island-hopping tour
items.blurb: Boat trips to Koh Ma, Chaloklum bay, or snorkelling and diving, with gear and lunch included. Price depends on the program and number of stops.

items.name: Drinks / party
items.blurb: Buckets and party-night drinks add up fast. On full moon nights there's a beach entry fee and drink prices run higher than usual — set a budget beforehand and it's easier to keep a lid on it.

blocks.html: Roughly speaking, backpackers can keep it to around 800-1,200 THB a day (not counting party nights), while if you go for a nicer room and hit the cafés often, you're looking at around 1,800-3,000 THB and up per day. All of this climbs in high season and around full moon nights.

items: Pick your timing — aim for Dec-Apr if you want good weather, avoid Oct-Nov if you're worried about rain.
Check the real full moon date on the organiser's page, then decide whether to join the party or skip it.
Book your boat and room ahead, especially around high season and party nights.
Sort out an international driving permit and helmet, and check that your travel insurance covers motorbikes.
Set a daily budget and keep party-night money separate; carry only the cash you'll use.
Photograph the bike's scratches before you take it, and keep valuables in the safe.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Koh Phangan?
faq.a: December through April has the best weather — clear skies, little rain, calm seas — ideal for diving and island-hopping. But it's high season, so it's crowded and rooms are pricey. October through November is the Gulf of Thailand's rainy season, with heavy rain and rough seas; avoid it if you don't want to take the risk.

faq.q: What are the Full Moon Party dates for 2026?
faq.a: The approximate announced dates are 29 Jun, 31 Jul, 28 Aug, 26 Sep, 27 Oct, 24 Nov, and 24 Dec, plus a New Year countdown party on the night of 31 Dec. But dates can shift if they fall on a major Buddhist holiday, so always confirm the real date on the organiser's page before booking.

faq.q: Do I need to book a room in advance?
faq.a: During high season, full moon nights, and long Thai holiday weekends, book several weeks ahead — especially on the Haad Rin side, where rooms fill fast and often have multi-night minimum stays. In the rainy season there's plenty of availability and prices drop, so booking only a short time ahead is fine.

faq.q: What's a daily budget for Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Backpackers can keep it to around 800-1,200 THB a day (not counting party nights). If you go for a nicer room and hit the cafés often, it's around 1,800-3,000 THB and up per day. None of this includes the boat ticket to the island, and it all climbs in high season and around full moon nights.

faq.q: Is riding a motorbike on Koh Phangan dangerous?
faq.a: There's a real risk, especially on the steep roads to Haad Rin and Thong Nai Pan, sand on the bends, dark roads at night, and drink-riding. Wear a helmet, carry a licence and insurance, ride slowly when you're not confident, and never ride drunk — if you've been drinking, take a shuttle back.
